claim: On Aug 10, 2026 Amazon MSK started to support in-place migration from Apache ZooKeeper to KRaft, so customers can migrate existing clusters to KRaft without provisioning new infrastructure, migrating data, or reconfiguring client applications. Kafka 3.9.x is the last version to support ZooKeeper, and Kafka 4.x only supports KRaft. This is not examinable yet.
question: Can an existing ZooKeeper-based MSK cluster move to KRaft in place, and since when?

values.display: in-place migration from Apache ZooKeeper to KRaft

qualifiers.condition: announced after the exam-readiness cutoff, so not examinable yet; first upgrade to Kafka 3.9.x if on an older version

evidence.quote: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) now supports in-place migration from Apache ZooKeeper to KRaft, enabling customers to migrate existing clusters to KRaft without provisioning new infrastructure, migrating data, or reconfiguring client applications.
Kafka 3.9.x is the last version to support ZooKeeper, and Kafka 4.x only supports KRaft.

evidence.heading: Amazon MSK now supports in-place migration from Apache ZooKeeper to KRaft

note: NOT EXAMINABLE YET (GA after 2026-07-15). Goes in 'Changed recently' only.

claim: On Jul 30, 2026 Amazon MSK Express brokers started to deliver data to Amazon S3 general purpose buckets as a fully managed capability. MSK Express supports throughput of up to 10 GB/s for data delivery to Amazon S3. This is not examinable yet.
question: Can MSK Express brokers deliver Kafka data to S3 without a connector, and since when?

values.display: up to 10 GB/s for data delivery to Amazon S3

qualifiers.condition: announced after the exam-readiness cutoff, so not examinable yet; available in every AWS Region where Express brokers are offered

evidence.quote: Amazon MSK Express brokers now delivers data to Amazon S3 general purpose buckets, providing a fully managed capability to deliver Apache Kafka data in Amazon S3 for downstream processing in the easiest and most reliable way.
MSK Express supports throughput of up to 10 GB/s for data delivery to Amazon S3, and manages routine operations such as capacity scaling and version upgrades without introducing delivery gaps.

evidence.heading: Amazon MSK Express brokers now delivers Apache Kafka data to Amazon S3

note: NOT EXAMINABLE YET (GA after 2026-07-15). Goes in 'Changed recently' only. Before this, the options were Firehose with MSK as a source (2023) or MSK Connect.

claim: On Jul 30, 2026 Amazon MSK Express brokers started to deliver data to streaming tables for Apache Iceberg, which continuously materializes Apache Kafka topics as Apache Iceberg tables on Amazon S3 Tables. This is not examinable yet.
question: Can MSK Express brokers deliver Kafka topics to Apache Iceberg tables, and since when?

evidence.quote: Amazon MSK Express brokers now deliver data to streaming tables for Apache Iceberg, a new capability that continuously materializes Apache Kafka topics as Apache Iceberg tables on Amazon S3 Tables.

evidence.heading: Amazon MSK Express brokers now deliver data to streaming tables for Apache Iceberg

note: NOT EXAMINABLE YET (GA after 2026-07-15). The change feed lists the Iceberg post (2026-07-30) next to the S3 post; its own id was not looked up.
